summary: Sarah McVie's public statements on social services center on dignity and equitable service delivery. In a 2019 post, McVie highlighted the scale of homelessness in Canada (235,000 people annually) and promoted Raising the Roof's #iGiveaDamn toque campaign to fund programs addressing homelessness. In 2026 posts, McVie framed social services through a dignity lens, stating that neglect of underserved residents diminishes the whole city and that focusing on dignity for all makes housing, commutes, and public spaces safer. McVie pledged, conditional on election, to prioritize under-serviced neighborhoods and improve service delivery across Toronto. Specific program details, funding mechanisms, or delivery models are not elaborated in the available records.

key_positions.stance: Acknowledges homelessness as a significant issue affecting hundreds of thousands of Canadians annually.
Frames social services around dignity for all residents, linking dignity to safer housing, commutes, and public spaces.
Supports prioritizing under-serviced neighborhoods while improving service delivery citywide.
States that systemic neglect of underserved residents diminishes the dignity of the whole city.

key_actions.action: Promoted Raising the Roof's #iGiveaDamn toque campaign to fund anti-homelessness programs in the GTA.
Pledged, if elected, to prioritize under-serviced neighborhoods and improve service delivery across Toronto.
